title: asymmetric-failover-stepdown-and-client-routing-corrections
body:
Summary:

During a partial outage in eu-west-1 on 2025-02-10 we observed an asymmetric failover where control-plane signals completed but a subset of customer clients continued to route to the degraded region for up to 14 minutes. This doc is a field note + corrective-runbook sketch capturing what went wrong, quick mitigations, verification checks, and follow-ups. Intended audience: SRE oncall, routing, edge, and infra owners.

What happened (timeline sketch):
- 16:02 UTC: upstream peering flap affected a subset of edge POPs in eu-west-1 causing variable egress latency and dropped connections.
- 16:03 UTC: automated regional health monitor flagged elevated p50/p95 for inference RPCs; circuit-breaker threshold breached.
- 16:04 UTC: smart-router policy (regional evacuation) initiated traffic diversion: incremental weight shifts from eu-west-1 -> eu-central-1 + us-east-1.
- 16:05-16:06 UTC: control-plane accepted the rollout and updated routing table; warm-standby KV preseed started for eu-central-1.
- 16:07 UTC: some edge nodes served stale DNS answers (high TTL cache) and continued to forward clients to eu-west-1.
- 16:16 UTC: ops noticed error spike for some customers and found asymmetric client distribution via trace sampling.
- 16:18 UTC: manual operator intervention performed a targeted DNS cache flush at edge, bumped route weights, and forced origin drains. Full symptom resolution by 16:22 UTC.

Root-cause hypotheses (iteration):
- TTL and stale-authoritative-propagation: a mixture of long-lived edge DNS caches + intermediate resolvers meant the routing switch did not reach all clients quickly.
- Incomplete KVCACHE pre-seed: warm-standby nodes in eu-central-1 began accepting traffic but were missing some customer-scoped prefix cache which caused elevated latencies and limited acceptance, delaying automated rollback and weight increases.
- Control-plane vs data-plane divergence: control-plane signaled traffic shift but not all data-plane proxies refreshed routing configs due to a throttled push mechanism and a simultaneous push failure in a subset of POPs.
- Edge peering oscillation amplified partial visibility: peering flap produced packet loss that made edge health checks show flakiness, triggering partial operators to mis-evaluate node health.

Immediate mitigation steps (operational checklist) - what to run when you see asymmetric client routing:
1) Triage and scope
   - Run: prometheus query: sum by(region) (rate(inference_requests_total[1m])) to see live client distribution.
   - Trace sample: pull a handful of traces with sampling id prefix "evac-" to map client IP -> edge POP -> origin region.
   - Confirm control-plane state: curl control-plane api /v1/route-policies/current to validate intended weights.
2) If control-plane != observed distribution:
   - Step A: Immediately increase weight to healthy regions by an aggressive increment (example: from 60/20/20 to 20/40/40) to bias new sessions away from bad region.
   - Step B: For customers with persistent connections, execute targeted edge cache invalidation. Operators with edge-admin access: run edgectl cache invalidate --zone eu-west-1 --type dns --label stale-answers.
   - Step C: TTL workarounds: push a transient authoritative TTL=30s for affected route prefix and publish change; monitor for propagation.
3) KVCACHE preseed health check
   - Query preseed job status: kubectl -n serving get jobs | grep kv-preseed-eu-central and kubectl logs on preseed pods. Look for per-tenant missing-prefix warnings.
   - If missing keys found: trigger kv-resync tool: tools/kv-resync --region eu-central-1 --tenants file:///tmp/missing-tenants.csv --priority high.
4) Data-plane push verification
   - For each POP, confirm agent last-config-reload via: curl http://edge-pop-status/<pop>/config | jq .last_reload_ts. Any pop older than event start -> consider manual agent restart: systemctl restart edge-proxy.
   - Check control-plane push queue backlog: redis-cli -n 6 LLEN push_queue. If backlog > 500, pause automated gradual rollouts and drain backlog manually.
5) Customer communication triage
   - For customers affected (identified by trace mapping), open ephemeral support channel and advise: short-lived region pin to eu-central-1 via customer override while we clean caches.

Verification checklist (how we know it's fixed):
- Request distribution matches intended weights for 5 consecutive 60s windows. (PromQL assertion attached).
- No 5xx spike in client-sampled traces originating in stale edge POPs for 10m.
- KVCACHE miss-rate drops to baseline (baseline defined per tenant in dashboard).
- Edge DNS cache hit-rate shows TTL refresh within 2 min window.
- End-to-end sample requests for a known customer route and model succeed within SLO.

Post-incident follow-ups (action items):
- Short-term (owner: Ethan Zhang, due 2025-03-01): implement an automated edge-dns-evict tool that can be targeted by region and by route-prefix; integrate into the runbook UI for oncall.
- Medium-term (owner: Carla Ruiz, due 2025-04-15): add per-pop config-reload telemetry and an alert if any pop lag >120s during a rollout.
- Medium-term (owner: Maya Patel, due 2025-05-01): expand kv-preseed to stream missing prefix metrics to Console with a per-tenant health badge so rollouts can be gated.
- Long-term (owner: Platform Eng, due 2025-07-01): investigate routing-change handshake: enforce a quick acknowledgement from data-plane agents before control-plane marks rollout step complete.

Runbook draft edits (concise commands to run)
- Observe distribution: curl -s "http://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=sum by(region)(rate(inference_requests_total[1m]))" | jq .data.result
- Find traces by client-ip: curl -s "http://tracing/api/search?query=client_ip:1.2.3.4&limit=50"
- Force edge cache invalidation (operator): edgectl --env prod invalidate-dns --region eu-west-1 --route-prefix /api/v1/infer --force
- Bump authoritative TTL (control-plane): curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://controlplane/api/routes/evac/ttl -d '{"ttl":30}'
- Restart edge proxy (last-resort): ssh edge-admin@<pop> sudo systemctl restart edge-proxy

Open questions / unresolved items to research:
- How many external resolvers held long-lived records beyond authoritative TTL bump? We need a measurement plan to estimate resolver stickiness (owner: Noah Green).
- Do some customers rely on long-lived WebSocket sessions that won't re-resolve DNS? If so, we must document a customer override flow to rehome existing sockets via proxy-level reconnect.
- Can we make kv-preseed idempotent and resumable per-tenant so that partial preseed won't create degraded acceptance windows?

Notes from operator and evidence snippets:
- Edgectl output (snippet):
  - pop eu-west-1: dns-cache-size=78k, dns-cache-hits=92.3%, last-refresh=2025-02-10T16:02:17Z
  - pop eu-west-3: last_reload_ts=2025-02-10T15:56:02Z (did not reload during rollout)
- Prometheus spike: p95 latency eu-west-1 inference RPCs 3.1s -> 12.4s between 16:02-16:06
- Trace sampling: 17% of sample traces still routed to eu-west-1 at 16:10 even though intended weight was <10%

Communication blurb for status page (draft):
"Intermittent edge connectivity in eu-west-1 caused increased inference latency for a subset of customers. We initiated a regional traffic rehome and completed mitigation actions to redistribute traffic; some clients continued to be routed due to cached DNS answers and persistent connections. All customers are receiving normal service; we are investigating caching and preseed gaps and will follow up with a detailed postmortem."

Appendix: suggested experiments to reduce recurrence
- Controlled TTL experiment: run a canary where authoritative TTL is set to 15s for a small route and measure end-to-end switch time across common resolver networks (400 clients, 3 regions).
- Push-ack protocol proof-of-concept: modify agent to ACK config version with nonce; require N acks before marking rollout step complete. Evaluate 99pct time-to-ack distribution.
- KVCACHE streaming resync: simulate partial preseed and measure service acceptance delta; goal: less than 2% request fail rate during preseed transitions.

References and helpful links:
- Related incident logs: confluence:regional-evacuation-fast-path-operator-scratchpad
- KB: edgectl reference: internal docs/edge/edgectl.md
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2123 (notes on TTL propagation fix)

Draft status and next steps:
- This is a working runbook + incident field note. Please add missing command snippets, validate user-facing blurb, and assign owners for action items above. After in_review we will convert the most stable steps into the canonical runbook entry under SRE Runbooks -> Regional Failover.
